content.title: DRAGONS DOWN: WILDLANDS
content.content:
![](/images/pdf/37f74aa0bbf43addc356a799f1c65d453770f235.jpeg)

![](/images/pdf/cb8d1a78f16dacefdd2092d9fa0cbe141ceb3400.jpeg)

Version 1.4. October 9, 2026

![](/images/pdf/3486f0f0a099b0ad2c78ad2473e124ce7773ac41.jpeg)

*“Pushing deeper into the wilderness, we found places few had dared to explore* *even before the dragons came. Dense thickets stretched beneath canopies of* *Green interspersed with wild hills. Hidden dangers were in every shadowed* *hollow. Yet there were rumors of forgotten places and strange peoples within. I* *decided to venture into these wildlands to discover what adventures await....”*

**Dragons Down: Wildlands** expands Dragons Down by introducing weather and two new Terrain Packs. New components for the Wildlands expansion are marked with a small ![inline](/images/pdf/b81beb4450eca6cfb341eeeb750e2790852f033e.jpeg) in one corner. Counters, round cardboard tokens, and Hero Chips do not have a mark.

content.title: Tangled Thickets
content.content:
- 6 Map Tiles
- X Terrain Pack Setup Card
- X Title Cards
- X Wilderness Tokens (*not counting blanks*)
- X Civilization Tokens
- X Civilization Location Tokens
- X Missions
- X Monster Chips
- X Native Chips

content.title: Hostile Hills
content.content:
- 6 Map Tiles
- X Terrain Pack Setup Card
- X Title Cards
- X Wilderness Tokens (*not counting blanks*)
- X Civilization Tokens
- X Civilization Location Token
- X Missions
- X Monster Chips
- X Native Chips

content.title: Additional Game Components
content.content:
- X Class Cards
- X Hero Chips and X Targeting Tokens
- X Treasure and Deep Treasure Cards
- X Specialized Merchant Tokens
- X Item Cards

content.title: Game Setup
content.content:
Players may choose from any of the Terrain Packs, including the two new packs introduced in the Wildlands expansion, in any combination. Shuffle the Map Tiles from the chosen Terrain Packs together to create the Map Tile stack as normal. Players may also select any Lineage and Class for any game of Dragons Down.

The Tangled Thickets Terrain Pack is a dangerous place, featuring four Treasure Sites filled with exotic treasures and protected by the dangers of the jungle.

The Hostile Hills Terrain Pack is a perilous land featuring three Treasure Sites, along with Monsters and Natives unique to its rugged terrain.

content.title: Thickets Clearings
content.content:
![float-right](/images/pdf/6b692a6f67fec1af8362c566414ab32a6f377109.jpeg) Tangled Thickets Map Tiles include Thickets Clearings, marked with a purple Thickets icon. Dense, overgrown foliage makes movement difficult and provides ample opportunities to hide.

Entering a Thickets Clearing costs 2 actions, even if flying. During the Action Phase, flying may not be used to enter or leave a Thickets Clearing except along connected paths. When entering a Tangled Thickets Map Tile by flying, a Hero may not land in a Thickets Clearing.

These restrictions on flying apply only during the Action Phase and have no effect during combat. If using the optional Terrain Effects rules, treat Thickets Clearings as Woods Clearings.

content.title: Hills Clearings
content.content:
![float-right](/images/pdf/61de902340045f769b72e2dd9d1f19ff62f36cc4.jpeg) Hostile Hills tiles introduce a new type of clearing called a Hills Clearing, marked with a brown Hills icon. Hills Clearings represent areas elevated above the surrounding lands.

Entering a Hills Clearing costs 2 actions unless the Hero is entering from another Hills Clearing or a Mountain Clearing. A Hero using flying movement pays only 1 action to enter a Hills Clearing.

The Hostile Hills include some unique monsters with special rules as spelled out in the Monster Manifest in the Appendix of these rules.

content.title: Civilization Tokens
content.content: The Wildlands expansion includes X new Civilization Tokens. When an empty token is revealed, it behaves the same as empty tokens in Dragons Down. When one of the tokens with a Merchant name is revealed, fill the location on the appropriate Merchant board with the listed numbers of treasures, items, and missions. The Merchant behaves exactly the same as a Merchant in Dragons Down.

content.title: Wilderness Tokens
content.content:
The Wildlands expansion adds 18 Wilderness Tokens (9 tokens for each new Terrain Pack). Mix each of these new tokens into the existing token piles. When moving or exploring a Hero may reveal one of the new tokens. Each new token type is explained below:

- ![float-right](/images/pdf/ddbeaaea8574600f879f4ea62511a4c3c9e72dc1.jpeg) **Discovery**: Draw another Hostile Hills Wilderness Token and place it in the Map Tile. The Hero rolls the two Mission Dice and receives the rewards indicated by the dice roll.

content.title: Sheltered and Unsheltered Heroes
content.content:
**Dragons Down: Eastern Reaches** introduces two optional rules, Terrain Effects Revisited and Weather, that use a new condition: Sheltered and Unsheltered Heroes. If neither optional rule is being used, this condition has no effect on gameplay and may be ignored.

A Hero is Sheltered while in a Clearing that meets any of the following conditions; otherwise, the Hero is Unsheltered. During a Move Action, determine whether the Hero is Sheltered or Unsheltered based on the Clearing being entered.

- Cave Clearing.

- Contains a Civilization Location.

- Contains a Treasure Site that the Hero has found, provided its Guardian is not present. *Exception: If using side 2 of the Terrain Setup Cards, the* *Chamber, Monolith, and Watchtower must also have been opened to* *provide shelter.*

content.title: OPTIONAL RULES
content.content: Optional rules allow players to customize their experience with Dragons Down. Most of these rules slightly increase the complexity of the game and may be mixed and matched in a modular fashion to maximize thematic immersion and enjoyment.

content.title: Weather
content.content:
Weather in Dragons Down introduces changing conditions that affect Heroes as they explore the realm. Each Weather Card represents a specific type of weather or effect, how long it remains in effect, and the effects it has on the game. Some Weather Cards are limited to certain seasons.

Weather can be used with any game modes or scenarios.

content.title: Weather Cards
content.content:
Weather Cards contain information on how it is applied in the game.

**Weather Type:** The name at the top of the card identifies the type of weather.

![](/images/pdf/ca37d61314b21eb8fa98ca7bb77ed4e12fefb87a.jpeg)

**Duration:** The numbered spaces show how many turns the weather lasts (this is also shown in the lower left of the card).

**Weather Reveal:** One of the Duration boxes on the Weather Card indicates when the next Weather Card is revealed.

**Game Effects:** These symbols show the rules that are in effect while this Weather Card is active. For example, the Cold Weather Card shown above indicates that a Hero who spends any portion of their turn Unsheltered must either spend an action or take a wound of their choice.

**Seasons:** The symbols along the bottom of the card indicate the seasons in which this type of weather can occur. The available seasons are, in order on the cards, Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter.

![Annotated weather card reference](/images/annotations/7a867ef512bc5f9a750bf0b3076c0257ea87c5d8.png)

content.title: Game Setup
content.content:
To include weather in a game, players first select a season, either by choice or randomly. Only one season is used for the entire game.

Remove all Weather Cards that do not show the chosen season symbol at the bottom of the card. Shuffle the remaining cards and deal 8 of them face-down to form the Weather Pile. Return all unused Weather Cards to the box without revealing them.

Reveal the top card of the Weather Pile and place it near the game board. Place a pink Status Cube on the first Duration box. This Weather Card is now active and its Game Effects apply.

content.title: Weather Progression
content.content:
At the end of the Battle Phase of each turn, check the active Weather Card.

If there is another Duration box, advance the pink Status Cube to that box. If the cube enters a box containing a Weather Reveal symbol, reveal the top card of the Weather Pile and place it next to the active Weather Card. This is the next Weather Card that will enter play, but it is not yet active. It is revealed to give players a glimpse of the weather to come for planning purposes.

It is important to ensure that all players understand the Game Effects of upcoming Weather Cards.

If there is no next Duration box, the active weather ends. If a next Weather Card has been revealed, it becomes the new active Weather Card. Place it on top of the previous Weather Card, leaving the number in the lower left corner of the previous card visible as a turn counter. Place the pink Status Cube on the first Duration box of the new active Weather Card. Its Game Effects apply to the next turn of the game.

If there is no next Weather Card when the active weather ends, the game ends. Process game end normally for the mode or scenario you are playing.

content.title: Weather Effects
content.content:
Effects due to Weather Cards are in addition to any other terrain effects. *For* *example, movement costs, wounds from Desert Clearings, etc.*

Each Weather Card is explained in detail in the Weather Card Manifest on page 4.

![](/images/pdf/3486f0f0a099b0ad2c78ad2473e124ce7773ac41.jpeg)

content.title: Enhanced Alert
content.content: When performing an Alert Action, in addition to rearranging equipment, the Hero chooses one of the following benefits. A Hero may perform multiple Alert Actions during a single turn. A Hero must choose a different alert type for each Alert Action.

content.title: Normal Alert
content.content: During combat this turn, the Hero may place +1 Speed Cube in each round of combat. Place a pink Status Cube on the Alert Box on the Hero Board to indicate that the Hero has chosen Normal Alert this turn.

content.title: Magic Alert
content.content:
Choose 1 healthy Magic Cube and place it in the Alert Box on the Hero Board. If the alerted Magic Cube is used to cast a Spell during combat this turn, that Spell gains +1 Attack Speed, even if all Attack Speed boxes are filled. At the end of the round in which the Spell is cast, move the alerted Magic Cube to the Wounded Box.

An alerted Magic Cube may not be placed in a Spell Box showing a wound symbol. If the alerted Magic Cube is not used to cast a Spell during combat that turn, return it to the Healthy Box.

content.title: Missile Alert
content.content: Place a pink Status Cube on the Ranged Attack icon of an equipped Ranged Weapon Card (not a Spell Card). A Hero may only have one Ranged Weapon Card alerted at a time. During combat this turn, when attacking with that weapon, if both Ranged Attack Dice results are negative, the Hero may reroll both dice. If only one, or none, of the Ranged Attack Dice results are negative, then they may not be rerolled.

content.title: Specialists
content.content:
![float-right](/images/pdf/0ac157d86509aa3f5b32be5dad738fd0d9f305c8.jpeg) Throughout the realm, Heroes may encounter remarkable Specialists whose rare talents provide assistance unavailable anywhere else. When using this optional rule, shuffle the Specialist Tokens and place them in a convenient location. Whenever an empty Civilization Token is drawn at a Civilization Location, replace it with a random Specialist Token.

Each Specialist offers a unique service or ability that Heroes may use when they encounter them. Specialists are not Merchants and provide none of the services that Heroes may normally perform. Specialists only offer their unique services, which may be purchased by performing a Trade Action with that Specialist.

The Base Price for each Specialist’s service is shown below and on their token. The Starting Price is 3 times the Base Price. Heroes may haggle following the standard Haggle rules using their lowest attribute.

All Specialists are explained in the Specialists Manifest on page 4.

content.title: Stubborn Guardians
content.content: Guardians return to the Monster Trays only when the Monsters Return arrow without the dot is rolled (on the Summoning Die from the Core ***Dragons Down*** Game). All other Monsters return when either Monsters Return arrow is rolled.

content.title: Shuttered Markets
content.content: While Monsters occupy a Clearing containing a Civilization Location, Heroes may not perform Trade Actions in that Clearing, except to swap possessions with another Hero.

content.title: Banished Heroes
content.content:
Heroes start the game banished. Set up the game normally for the chosen game mode. If playing in Exploration Mode without the Ruthless Riverlands, place a random Wilderness Map Tile instead of a Civilization Map Tile.

After setting up the map, randomly select one of the Wilderness Map Tiles placed during setup. Place each Hero (or Adventure Party) in a random Clearing on the selected Map Tile.

When the first Player Token is revealed on the first turn of the game, immediately reveal and place a Wilderness Token as if the Hero had just entered the Map Tile.

For added difficulty, combine this optional rule with the Wits Only optional rule from the **Dragons Down** Core Game.

content.title: Terrain Effects Revisited
content.content:
Terrain Effects were introduced in **Dragons Down: Eastern Reaches** and give additional importance to individual Clearing types. These optional rules are repeated here to include the new Clearing types and revise the conditions under which Heroes may ignore Terrain Effects.

The following Terrain Effects apply whenever a Hero occupies a Clearing of the corresponding type. A Sheltered Hero may **choose** to ignore Terrain Effects.

- **Thickets and Woods Clearings:** Dense foliage provides ample concealment opportunities. Heroes attempting to Hide receive the benefits of Sneaking, even if they did not perform a Sneak Action.

- **Plains Clearing:** The open, featureless terrain offers few places to hide. Heroes attempting to Hide do not receive the benefits of a Sneak Action taken this turn. Magical effects from Treasures and Spells still apply.

- **Swamps Clearing:** The diseased and fetid nature of swamps makes healing nearly impossible. Heroes may not perform a Rest Action.

- **Desert Clearings:** Desert Clearings are hot, barren, and offer little protection from the elements. Heroes ending their Action Phase in a Desert Clearing must immediately suffer 1 wound of their choice.

- **Caves, Hills, Mountains, and River Clearings:** No additional effects.

All normal terrain rules remain in effect, even when a Hero is Sheltered.

- Movement costs.

- Loss of 1 Action per turn in Cave Clearings.

- All movement and other rules governing River Clearings.

- Restricted Flying movement in Thickets Clearings.

content.title: Broom Hand
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/b96aab0401ae8dc9b1494218992bedde12881702.jpeg) Base Price: 2 Gold. Starting Price: 6 Gold. Fly to an adjacent Map Tile of the your without spending a Move Action. All other flying rules apply.

content.title: Chanter
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/2d23543eb48b3e42592c8fdfa49a60abf9321de6.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Enchant a Map Tile up to 2 Map Tiles away using a magic color of your choice.

content.title: City Mancer
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/85af05104f6503eb3c82ceddef0526388da17c7b.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Move to any revealed Civilization Location of your choice without spending a Move Action.

content.title: Curator
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/f44838e5b21e5dac81b8ee1b6aeaf747f71a3f5e.jpeg) Base Price: 5 Gold. Starting Price: 15 Gold. Draw 1 random Treasure Card from the Treasure Deck.

content.title: Earth Mover
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/45c96c24757ad5900626b5dab1bc36a04722f6c1.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Rotate the Map Tile containing the Earth Mover, or an adjacent Map Tile, to any legal orientation. After rotating, all paths must connect to paths, and all non-paths must connect to non-paths, on adjacent Map Tiles.

content.title: Fencer
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/b31d72a66e55ea9dbd585e6ccf096c2dcaa8b1b3.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Draw 1 random Item Card from the Item Deck.

content.title: Gate Mage
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/a5dad506f1da40018a1d4037dc7416f8418e647b.jpeg) Base Price: 2 Gold. Starting Price: 6 Gold. Move to a Clearing of your choice containing a revealed Gate without spending a Move Action.

content.title: Healer
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/bc8f0a400a48d5a9e02f0ac10536e9d275e0dc60.jpeg) Base Price: 1 Gold per cube. Starting Price: 3 Gold per cube. Choose how many cubes to heal before rolling any Haggle Dice. Haggle to determine the price per cube, then multiply that price by the number of cubes healed.

content.title: Magus
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/afaedb32ffc83973151deed55cf7e26d965246f7.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold + the Spell’s Price. Starting Price: 3 times the Base Price. Learn 1 Spell Card attached to an equipped Treasure Card. Does not require rolling the Learn Dice.

content.title: Pathfinder
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/427f2e9c24a7d7ea2238523ed78ccbdfde333674.jpeg) Base Price: 2 Gold. Starting Price: 6 Gold. Find 1 face-up Hidden Path of your choice on a Map Tile up to 2 Map Tiles away from the Pathfinder.

content.title: Telecrafter
content.content:
![float-right](/images/pdf/a8ff0561b27b941956878f0637414ed618cc5faa.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Teleport to a random Clearing on a Map Tile of your choice up to 2 Map Tiles away.

![](/images/pdf/ca37d61314b21eb8fa98ca7bb77ed4e12fefb87a.jpeg)

content.title: Clear
content.content: Lasts 6 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 5. No effect on gameplay.

content.title: Clouds
content.content: Lasts 5 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. No effect on gameplay.

content.title: Cold
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. A Hero must spend 1 Action to stay warm or take 1 wound of their choice unless they are Sheltered at the end of their Action Phase.

content.title: Cool
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 3. No effect on gameplay.

content.title: Corrupted
content.content:
Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. At the beginning of each turn, randomly select one magic color. Until the end of the turn, magic cubes of the selected color may not be used for any purpose, and no enchantments of that color may occur. Immediately remove all existing enchantments of the selected color.

These restrictions also apply to Monsters and Natives, but do not affect a Dragon’s Fireball.

content.title: Cursed
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. A Hero must take 1 wound of their choice or receive a random Curse unless they are Sheltered at the end of their Action Phase.

content.title: Dark Omens
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. Roll the Summoning Dice twice during Monster Activation.

content.title: Deep Snow
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. A Hero must spend 1 additional Action when moving into a Clearing where they would be Unsheltered, even if Swimming, but not if Flying.

content.title: Dreamlike
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 2. All Heroes receive +1 action during their Action Phase.

content.title: Enchanted
content.content:
Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 3. At the beginning of each turn, randomly select one magic color. Until the end of the turn, all Map Tiles are considered enchanted with that magic color. Ignore all other enchantments and enchantment effects. Do not flip any Map Tiles due to this weather card.

Map Tiles may still be enchanted normally, including placing Magic Cubes and flipping Map Tiles. However, these enchantments have no effect until Enchanted weather ends.

![](/images/pdf/3486f0f0a099b0ad2c78ad2473e124ce7773ac41.jpeg)

content.title: Fog
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. During each Search Action, Heroes must reroll one successful search result.

content.title: Gloom
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. All Heroes receive -1 action during their Action Phase.

content.title: High Winds
content.content: Lasts 5 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. All Ferrying, Flying, and Swimming movement actions require +1 action.

content.title: Hot
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 3. A Hero must take 1 wound of their choice unless they are Sheltered at the end of their Action Phase.

content.title: Icebound
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. All Swamp and River Clearings are treated as Plains Clearings, including when using the Terrain Effects optional rule. No Ferry Movement is allowed. A Hero must spend 1 action to stay warm or take 1 wound of their choice unless they are Sheltered at the end of their Action Phase.

content.title: Primal
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 3. Both the Wandering and Local Monster Number Die summon one additional Monster.

content.title: Rain
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 3. A Hero may not perform a Rest Action while Unsheltered.

content.title: Snow Storms
content.content:
Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. A Hero must spend 1 additional Action or take 1 wound of their choice when moving into a Clearing where they would be Unsheltered, even if Flying or Swimming. No Ferry Movement is allowed.

When playing Adventure Party Cooperative Mode, the Party Leader chooses whether to spend the additional Action or take a wound. This choice applies to all members of the party.

content.title: Thunder Storms
content.content: Lasts 4 turns. Reveal the next Weather Card on turn 4. A Hero must take 1 wound of their choice if they are Unsheltered in a Mountain, Plains, River, or Swamp Clearing at the end of their Action Phase.

content.title: Diviner (Shard Charge)
content.content: Diviner can channel magical energy into a shard they always have with them, enhancing its power. When taking an Alert action may place a healthy magic cube on the shard space of their class card (returning any cube already there to their healthy box), in lieu of the normal Alert action. During combat, this cube counts as two cubes of the same color when casting spells. If the cube is wounded during combat, the effect is immediately canceled. At the end of combat the cube is returned to the Hero’s healthy box.

content.title: Gravesworn (Dead Speech)
content.content:
The Gravesworn is protector and researcher of all things undead. Undead do not block or target the Gravesworn, nor may the Gravesworn, or their hired natives, target the undead (including attacks that target the entire Clearing like Fiery Chasm or Earthquake). The Gravesworn may not loot treasure sites whose protectors are undead Guardians. The Gravesworn may have one undead Monster as a minion (hired native) at any time as follows.

Using a normal Hire Action, the Gravesworn must haggle to reduce the hire price to 1x. The Gravesworn only fails in a haggle attempt by rolling a door symbol. The Gravesworn pays no actual cost to hire an undead Monster. All other Hired Natives rules apply (From **Dragons Down: Natives & Legends**). Monsters belong to no group. Thus, a closed door result on a haggle attempt does not prevent the Gravesworn from hiring other undead Monsters on that same turn, even the same Monster type. The Gravesworn loses Fame when their minion is killed.

The Gravesworn may not attempt to hire a Monster while they already have a minion. The Gravesworn may not fly using a hired minion (unlike the Beastmaster).

content.title: Inquisitor (King’s Justice)
content.content: The inquisitor speaks with the king’s voice and act with the king’s hand. The inquisitor does not draw outlaw tokens for any reason.

content.title: Shaman (Totemic Projection)
content.content:
The Shaman casts their spirit beyond the bounds of their body, sensing what lies unseen. Shamans may perform a search action in an adjacent map tile containing no wilderness or civilization tokens. Upon a successful search, place a matching token(s) face-down in the tile. The hero may look it, but may not reveal it. No special tokens are triggered.

If playing using the exploration rules, the hero may explore as if in a mountain clearing to place a map tile, but must search in order to place tokens per the rules explained above.

content.title: The Cult
content.content:
No one really knows who leads the cult and their members are hard to distinguish. At the end of any combat round in which the Cult Leader is killed, replace the dead Cult Leader chip with a Cult Member chip.

- If any Cult Members are still alive in the combat, randomly choose one and replace its chip with the Cult Leader chip with the same side facing up. Place the replaced Cult Member chip in the Hero’s Trophy Pile.

- If no Cult Members remain in the combat, replace the dead Cult Leader chip with a Cult Member chip from the Monster Tray.

- If there are no Cult Members remaining in either the combat or the Monster Tray, congratulations, you killed the actual Cult Leader. Place the Cult Leader chip in the Hero’s Trophy Pile.

content.title: Grim Wretch
content.content: The Grim Wretch casts Panoply on itself. If Panoply is already active on the Grim Wretch, ignore the effect.

content.title: Jaguar Warriors
content.content:
Jaguar Warriors summon to both the Enclave and The Wilds Map Tile. When summoning to the Enclave, summon a number of randomly determined Jaguar Warriors equal to the sum of the two Summoning Number Dice.

While in the same Clearing as the Enclave, all Jaguar Warriors are considered Guardians. Otherwise, they are treated as normal Monsters.

content.title: Revenant
content.content:
The Revenant casts Foresight while on the front side of its chip, even if all Heroes in the Clearing are hidden. Each time the Revenant casts Foresight, set one of the Summoning Dice as follows, in order:

- **First Foresight:** Set the Local Monster Symbol Die to the symbol matching the Map Tile where the Revenant is located.

- **Second Foresight:** Set the Wandering Monster Symbol Die to the symbol matching the Map Tile where the Revenant is located.

- **Third Foresight:** Set the Local Monster Number Die to its highest numbered side.

- **Fourth Foresight:** Set the Wandering Monster Number Die to its highest numbered side.

- **Fifth Foresight:** The spell has no effect.

content.title: Wyvern
content.content: The Wyvern is considered a dragon for all game effects. For example, its Fireball is not a spell, like all dragons.

content.title: Unique Monsters
content.content:
All Guardians, the Cult Leader, Jaguar Champion, and Jaguar Priest are considered unique Monsters. Unique Monsters are immune to some game effects, such as being selected for the Shape Shift spell.

![](/images/pdf/ca37d61314b21eb8fa98ca7bb77ed4e12fefb87a.jpeg)

content.title: Aegis of Radiance
content.content: Epic Treasure. Armor. Armor Value 2. Weight 2. Adds +1 Maneuver Speed.

content.title: Aftershock
content.content: Epic Treasure. Melee Weapon. If this weapon hits its target, may give 1 Wound to any other unhidden Hero, Native, or Monster in the Clearing, but not the target of the original attack.

content.title: Boots of Displacement
content.content: Double the base attack length of all equipped Melee Weapons.

content.title: Burrow King’s Thing
content.content: May use any Blue Hidden Paths without first finding them. Using a Hidden Path does not cause it to be found.

content.title: Chameleon Creme
content.content: One-time Use. May reroll one Monster Die during a Hide attempt made during the Cleanup Step of Combat.

content.title: Curios
content.content:
One-Time Use. Grants one Action Cube of the indicated color. This cube is removed at the beginning of the Combat Phase of the following turn. Any Spell learned using a Magic Cube granted by a Curio remains learned after that cube is removed, but may only be cast with a Magic Cube of the matching color.

- **Curio of Conjuration:** Blue Magic Cube

- **Curio of Fay:** Yellow Magic Cube

- **Curio of Maneuver:** Brown Speed Cube

- **Curio of Might:** Red Might Cube

- **Curio of Nature:** Green Magic Cube

- **Curio of Power:** Purple Magic Cube

- **Curio of Righteousness:** White Magic Cube

- **Curio of the Black Arts:** Black Magic Cube

- **Curio of Tricks:** Gray Magic Cube

- **Curio of Wizardry:** Any Magic Cube of the Hero’s choice.

content.title: Diviner of Vourdanos
content.content: May reroll one Search Die once per Search Action while in Hills Clearings.

content.title: Drums of the Stampede
content.content: One-time use. Move all Monsters in the Hero’s Clearing to adjacent Clearings using normal or River Paths, but not Hidden Paths. The Hero chooses the destination Clearing for each Monster.

content.title: Elven Etchings
content.content:
May use any Green Hidden Paths without first finding them. Using a Hidden Path does not cause it to be found.

![](/images/pdf/3486f0f0a099b0ad2c78ad2473e124ce7773ac41.jpeg)

content.title: Eye of the Basilisk
content.content: Epic Treasure. Once per combat, during the Attack Resolution Step, may make one additional attack against any unhidden target that is targeting the Hero. This attack causes 1 Wound, has an Attack Length of 35, and uses the Hero’s Attack Speed to determine whether it hits. May resolve this attack before or after the normal attack.

content.title: Heartwood Totem
content.content: May reroll one Search Die once per Search Action while in Thickets Clearings.

content.title: Horizon Hexmark
content.content: May use any Gray Hidden Paths without first finding them. Using a Hidden Path does not cause it to be found.

content.title: Hourglass of Echoes
content.content: One-time use. When using a One-Time Use Treasure or Item, may discard the Hourglass of Echoes instead. The Treasure or Item being used is not discarded.

content.title: Ledger of Promises
content.content: When revealed, draw and attach 4 Missions to the Ledger of Promises. While equipped, may complete these Missions as if they were the Hero’s active Missions. These Missions do not count against the Hero’s 2 Mission limit.

content.title: Oracle Lens
content.content: Epic Treasure. May perform an Alert Action to look at the Treasure Cards in any 1 Treasure Site the Hero has found that is in their Clearing.

content.title: Parley Heart
content.content: Choose 1 enemy. That enemy may not target the Hero for the duration of combat unless the Hero first targets them.

content.title: Phylact of Renewal
content.content: Epic Treasure. If at least 1 cube is wounded, may perform an Alert Action to permanently remove any number of equipped or Backpack Treasure Cards from the game. For each regular Treasure Card removed, heal 1 wounded cube. For each Epic Treasure Card removed, heal up to 3 wounded cubes.

content.title: Ravager’s Flail
content.content: Melee Weapon. One required Might Box on this card is automatically filled and does not count against the Hero’s Cube Limit.

content.title: Ring of Reaching
content.content: Adds +5 to the Base Attack Length of all attacks.

content.title: Root Striders
content.content: Epic Treasure. May enter Swamp and Thickets Clearings for 1 action.

content.title: Rot Charm
content.content:
May use any Yellow Hidden Paths without first finding them. Using a Hidden Path does not cause it to be found.

![](/images/pdf/fd56ee5d2ef930ee310c3178a05dd688f3e792c2.png)

content.title: Silver Tongue
content.content: The final price paid during a Hire Action, after all haggling, is reduced by 1 Gold, to a minimum of 0.

content.title: Skyroad Sigil
content.content: May use any Purple Hidden Paths without first finding them. Using a Hidden Path does not cause it to be found.

content.title: Spinewhisper
content.content: Melee Weapon. When attacking a target that is not targeting the Hero, this attack occurs at +1 Attack Speed.

content.title: Stone of the New Path
content.content: One-Time Use. Flip the current Map Tile without enchanting it.

content.title: Stone Giant’s Warbelt
content.content: Epic Treasure. Once per combat, may increase the damage of 1 Melee Attack by 1. When used, immediately wound 1 cube of the Hero’s choice.

content.title: Stoneknuckle Gloves
content.content: Melee Weapon. Equipped in both hand positions instead of a weapon position. The required Might Box is automatically filled and does not require a Might Cube. May be equipped at the same time as another weapon. When attacking with the Stoneknuckle Gloves, place a pink Status Cube on this card to indicate that it is being used instead of the equipped Weapon Card.

content.title: Thornhide Brigandine
content.content: Epic Treasure. Armor. When a Melee Attack hits the Hero, the attacker also suffers 1 Wound.

content.title: Titan Steppers
content.content: Epic Treasure. May enter Hills and Mountain Clearings for 1 action.

content.title: To Do List
content.content: When revealed, draw and attach 2 Missions to the To Do List. While equipped, may complete these Missions as if they were the Hero’s active Missions. These Missions do not count against the Hero’s 2 Mission limit.

content.title: Veilpiercer
content.content: Epic Treasure. Ranged Weapon. Does not lose sword icons when striking Armor.

content.title: Venom of the Thousand Bites
content.content: One-time use. Attacks by this Hero gain +2 swords for the duration of Combat.

content.title: Whisper Pin
content.content: One-time use. Acts as a one-time use Skeleton Key. For example, opening the Monolith or Chamber, avoiding hidden traps at the Secret Cache, Hideout, or Wrecked Wagons or avoiding a wound at the Lost Captain’s Locker.

content.title: Windswept Mantle
content.content: +1 Maneuver Speed against all Ranged Attacks.

content.title: Wyvern Hide Armor
content.content: Epic Treasure. Armor. Armor Value 2. Weight 1. Blocks up to two sword icons.

content.title: Broom Hand
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/b96aab0401ae8dc9b1494218992bedde12881702.jpeg) Base Price: 2 Gold. Starting Price: 6 Gold. Fly to an adjacent Map Tile of the your without spending a Move Action. All other flying rules apply.

content.title: Chanter
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/2d23543eb48b3e42592c8fdfa49a60abf9321de6.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Enchant a Map Tile up to 2 Map Tiles away using a magic color of your choice.

content.title: City Mancer
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/85af05104f6503eb3c82ceddef0526388da17c7b.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Move to any revealed Civilization Location of your choice without spending a Move Action.

content.title: Curator
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/f44838e5b21e5dac81b8ee1b6aeaf747f71a3f5e.jpeg) Base Price: 5 Gold. Starting Price: 15 Gold. Draw 1 random Treasure Card from the Treasure Deck.

content.title: Earth Mover
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/45c96c24757ad5900626b5dab1bc36a04722f6c1.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Rotate the Map Tile containing the Earth Mover, or an adjacent Map Tile, to any legal orientation. After rotating, all paths must connect to paths, and all non-paths must connect to non-paths, on adjacent Map Tiles.

content.title: Fencer
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/b31d72a66e55ea9dbd585e6ccf096c2dcaa8b1b3.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Draw 1 random Item Card from the Item Deck.

content.title: Gate Mage
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/a5dad506f1da40018a1d4037dc7416f8418e647b.jpeg) Base Price: 2 Gold. Starting Price: 6 Gold. Move to a Clearing of your choice containing a revealed Gate without spending a Move Action.

content.title: Healer
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/bc8f0a400a48d5a9e02f0ac10536e9d275e0dc60.jpeg) Base Price: 1 Gold per cube. Starting Price: 3 Gold per cube. Choose how many cubes to heal before rolling any Haggle Dice. Haggle to determine the price per cube, then multiply that price by the number of cubes healed.

content.title: Magus
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/afaedb32ffc83973151deed55cf7e26d965246f7.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold + the Spell’s Price. Starting Price: 3 times the Base Price. Learn 1 Spell Card attached to an equipped Treasure Card. Does not require rolling the Learn Dice.

content.title: Pathfinder
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/427f2e9c24a7d7ea2238523ed78ccbdfde333674.jpeg) Base Price: 2 Gold. Starting Price: 6 Gold. Find 1 face-up Hidden Path of your choice on a Map Tile up to 2 Map Tiles away from the Pathfinder.

content.title: Telecrafter
content.content: ![float-right](/images/pdf/a8ff0561b27b941956878f0637414ed618cc5faa.jpeg) Base Price: 3 Gold. Starting Price: 9 Gold. Teleport to a random Clearing on a Map Tile of your choice up to 2 Map Tiles away.
